newsitem.title: USA: Netanyahu - "nothing definitive" in Clinton talks.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu - "nothing definitive" in Clinton talks.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Monday "nothing definitive" had come from his talks with President Bill Clinton and insisted it was the Palestinians not the Israelis who were breaking Middle East peace accords.

"I come here with absolutely clean hands," Netanyahu said at a news conference after a two-hour talk with Clinton. "I was elected with a promise to keep Oslo. We keep it," he said, referring to the Oslo negotiations that laid down the framework peace accord between Israel and the Palestinians.

He alleged bitterly that the Palestinians had succeeded in painting Israel as "the heavy" in the recent breakdown of their peace talks, saying: "Israel, which keeps the Oslo accords is accused of violating it. The Palestinian side, which violates the accords, is credited with keeping it. And that I think is an obstacle to peace."

The United States has made clear it too opposes the decision of Netanyahu's government to build new Jewish housing in mainly Arab East Jerusalem, a move that undermined the talks and has led to renewed street violence. Netanyahu said again on Monday before his White House visit that the housing construction was Israel's right and would continue.
Like Clinton, who referred to the talks as "frank" and "candid" -- terms that usually indicate a sharp clash of views in diplomatic terminology -- Netanyahu would give no details of their dicussions.

"These are preliminary discussions," he said. "Nothing formal and nothing definitive was said and I'm sure we'll have the opportunity to continue these exchanges of views in the coming days and weeks." Clinton was expected to meet with a Palestinian delegation later this week before deciding the next U.S. step as Middle East mediator.
